description: I’m passionate about space exploration, astronomy, science communication, and storytelling. I’m particularly interested in the fascinating stories behind NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars, and how these objects represent important milestones in humanity’s journey into space.
summary:
Have you ever wondered what happens to the machines and robots we leave behind in space? In this project, I will be exploring the forgotten space technology left behind on the Moon, Mars, and other places beyond Earth. These machines were sent into space with important missions, and each one has its own story, purpose, and discoveries. Through this project, I aim to bring these forgotten explorers back to life and show how they helped us learn more about space and the universe. Let's take a journey into the past and discover the stories behind these incredible machines!


This project is designed for complete beginners, with simple explanations and an accessible, storybook-style slide format that makes learning easy, enjoyable, and engaging.
At the heart of this project is the human side of space exploration. Behind every spacecraft, robot, and mission are people who dreamed, imagined, designed, built, and dared to explore the unknown. We will look at these forgotten machines with curious minds and love-filled eyes, remembering that they are more than just hardware. They are reminders of human dreams, courage, curiosity, failures, achievements, and our endless desire to discover what lies beyond Earth.
The goal is not simply to teach people about space technology, but to help them understand, appreciate, and feel a connection to the stories behind it.
details: This story is designed for primary school students (ages 5–10), translating complex space engineering into playful, accessible storytelling through a visual, storybook-style slide deck that pairs simple language with real NASA photography. Rather than covering every mission broadly, the narrative focuses on specific, iconic pieces of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars—such as the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, and the Ingenuity helicopter. By giving each machine a friendly nickname and highlighting their individual "perspectives" as brave robotic scouts, the story connects how their specialized hardware operated to the groundbreaking scientific discoveries they made for humanity.
